This guide uses the package datasets to express special mean-direction curves
and then fit repeated orientations from the same animal. The introductory
guide covers the common interface; this guide concentrates on parameter
interpretation and the change of sampling unit in a grouped model.

```{r}
library(CircularRegression)

data(bison)

d <- bison[seq_len(180), c("y.dir", "y.prec", "x.meadow", "z.meadow")]
d <- na.omit(d)
```

The response `y.dir` and angular covariates are in radians. The modifier
`z.meadow` is non-negative and enters through the weighted term
`x.meadow:z.meadow`.

## Select a Reference Direction

The homogeneous angular model fixes one plain angular term as the reference.
The package can select the reference direction using the empirical mean-cosine
criterion.

```{r}
ref <- select_reference_angle(
  y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow,
  data = d
)
ref
```

## Fit Homogeneous and Consensus Models

The homogeneous model can be fitted directly once the reference is known.

```{r}
fit_hom <- angular(
  y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow,
  data = d,
  reference = c("name", ref$ref_name)
)

summary(fit_hom)
```

The consensus model estimates one concentration-like coefficient for each
directional term.

```{r}
fit_cons <- consensus(
  y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow,
  data = d
)

summary(fit_cons)
```

The default high-level workflow fits the consensus model first, then fits the
homogeneous model with the selected reference direction.

```{r}
fit_two <- angular_two_step(
  y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow,
  data = d
)

coef(fit_two)
```

The coefficient for `x.meadow:z.meadow` is interpreted relative to the selected
reference direction. In this subset, its sign and magnitude describe how the
weighted meadow direction contributes to the fitted mean resultant vector after
the reference direction has coefficient one.

## Predictions and Residuals

Predictions are angles in radians. Residuals are wrapped circular differences.

```{r}
new_d <- d[seq_len(5), c("y.prec", "x.meadow", "z.meadow")]

predict(fit_hom, newdata = new_d)
head(fitted(fit_hom))
head(residuals(fit_hom))
```

A lightweight base-R residual plot is often sufficient for a first diagnostic
check.

```{r, fig.alt="Wrapped residuals from a homogeneous bison model against fitted direction, with zero marked."}
plot(
  fitted(fit_hom),
  residuals(fit_hom),
  xlab = "Fitted direction",
  ylab = "Circular residual",
  pch = 19,
  col = "gray30"
)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

## Special-Case Wrappers

The special-case wrappers keep the two-step fitting machinery but return
natural-parameter summaries for model forms used in the circular-regression
literature.

```{r}
mean_fit <- meanDirectionModel(
  data = d["y.dir"],
  response = "y.dir"
)

dec_fit <- decentredPredictorModel(
  data = d[c("y.dir", "y.prec")],
  response = "y.dir",
  w = "y.prec"
)

pres_fit <- presnellModel(
  data = na.omit(bison[500:579, c("y.dir", "z.gap")]),
  response = "y.dir",
  w = "z.gap"
)

jam_fit <- jammalamadakaModel(
  data = d[c("y.dir", "y.prec")],
  response = "y.dir",
  w = "y.prec"
)

mean_fit$natural_parameters
dec_fit$natural_parameters
pres_fit$natural_parameters
jam_fit$natural_parameters
```

For affine and first-harmonic curves, the ratios alone are not enough:
`natural_orientation` gives the sign by which both vector components must be
multiplied before calling `atan2()`. Natural covariances use analytic
Jacobians and require stable, identifiable parameterizations. Equality of a
mean curve does not imply equality with a projected-normal probability model.

## Random-Intercept Fit

The `sandhopper_trials` data contain five escape orientations per animal.
Each row is one observed trial, with angles in radians. The model uses the
sun azimuth as the reference and weights the wind direction by wind speed.
The term `(1 | Anim)` gives each animal its own random shift in mean direction.

```{r}
data(sandhopper_trials)

fit_re <- angular_re(
  escape ~ sun + wind:wind_speed + (1 | Anim),
  data = sandhopper_trials
)

fit_re$fit_status
coef(fit_re)
```

By default, `angular_re()` omits trials with missing model variables. This fit
uses `r length(fit_re$cluster)` trials from `r length(fit_re$ranef)` animals.
See `?sandhopper_trials` for the source and the preparation script.

The marginal prediction uses the fixed effects. The conditional prediction
reads `Anim` in `newdata` and adds the estimated shift for that animal.

```{r}
first_trial <- sandhopper_trials[1, ]
c(
  marginal = predict(fit_re, newdata = first_trial, type = "marginal"),
  conditional = predict(fit_re, newdata = first_trial, type = "conditional")
)
head(ranef.angular_re(fit_re))
```

The two concentration parameters describe dispersion on the circle. The
cluster-robust standard errors assume independent animals and are asymptotic
in their number. Conditional residuals reflect the estimation of the random
intercepts.
